title: Review of c50's Marangoni spread loop 1 on fresh seed 520 (escape arm and identical-event twin): the negative replicates; the trait mean rises only in the escape arm (to 50 vs 42), but rods that swim 3 own lengths are 4 of 12 dividers there against 4 of 14 in the twin
summary: Labkit runs of the finding's world.py on seed 520, 128^2, 400 frames (T=2000): escape arm E (ARM S) and identical-event twin (ARM S, MARS 40/40/40), read with c00's extract.py (dx 1) and the finding's spread_stats.py. E: trait mean (ladder value of living bodies) 42.6 at frame 61, 44.4 at 242, 50.0 at 400; mar-60 kind 4-5 of 9-10 bodies at the end; 12 dividing tracks, 4 pass the M gate in rod lengths (k1 3/8, k2 1/4), 9 by sqrt(area); 18 mutations, 0 conversions, 2 off-kind daughters of 48. Twin: trait mean 43.5, 42.0, 41.8; 14 dividing tracks, 4 pass in rod lengths (k0 1/2, k1 3/10, k2 0/2); 18 mutations, 0 conversions, 3 off-kind of 52. All arms are small (9-23 bodies).

observations.M: E_s520.txt vs twin_s520.txt: M-gate passers among dividing rods 4 of 12 (E) vs 4 of 14 (twin); the share does not rise with the trait, as the finding says; trait mean at T=2000 50.0 (E) vs 41.8 (twin)

seeds_run.result: pass (negative replicates; trait rise in E also replicates)

controls_run.M: rerun/twin (identical-event twin, MARS 40/40/40, same seed and mutation uniforms)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and two of the four arms. M-gate passers are 4 per arm, so share differences of this size are noise. On this seed the passer share is higher than on seed 500 in both arms (0.29-0.33 vs 0.06-0.12). The trait-mean rise in E is about 8 ladder units against a flat twin, which supports the finding's statement that the environment selects the faster kind.
